title: The Treasure That Sank Beneath Pride
intro: Imagine standing before piles of wealth so vast that merely carrying the keys would exhaust a group of strong individuals. Around you, voices urge humility and remembrance, yet pride grows louder than gratitude. What happens when bounty becomes a test and arrogance seals the outcome?
clues: I was from among the people of Musa, yet I transgressed against them.
I was granted treasures so immense that the keys to them would burden a band of strong men.
I was advised by my people not to exult and to seek the Hereafter without forgetting my share of this world.
I claimed that what I possessed was given to me only because of knowledge I had.
I paraded before my people in adornment, and those desiring worldly life wished for the like of what I had.
I was swallowed by the earth along with my dwelling, and none could help me nor could I help myself.

identity.label: Who Am I?
options: Qarun
Namrud
Jalut
Azar
Qabil

trial.label: Trial/Event
options: Boasted of wealth and denied Allah's favor despite counsel
Challenged Ibrahim about giving life and death
Led an army against Talut and Dawud
Carved idols for the people to worship
Killed a brother out of envy over an offering
trial.answer: Boasted of wealth and denied Allah's favor despite counsel

location.label: Key Element
options: Keys to immense treasures
The Ark of the Covenant
A golden calf of adornments
A dam between two mountains
Eleven stars in a dream

outcome.label: Outcome
options: Swallowed by the earth with dwelling and wealth
Drowned in the sea while pursuing Musa
Struck down by a stone from Dawud's sling
Destroyed by a mighty blast for hamstringing a she-camel
Turned into apes for breaking the Sabbath
outcome.answer: Swallowed by the earth with dwelling and wealth

arabic: فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٍۢ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنتَصِرِينَ
verse: And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allāh, nor was he of those who [could] defend themselves. (28:81)
